entries.summary: K8 owner cancels are idempotent and its refusals carry codes (#1405). cancelTurn returns TurnCancelResult { turnId, result, conclusion? } and cancelDelegation returns DelegationCancelResult { delegationId, result, verdict? }, in the shape of cancelHostIntent and read from the ledger, so a replay and a restart give the same answer: cancelled (this call committed the cancel), cancel_pending (an earlier cancel has no terminal yet) or already_settled (the target had ended, with its conclusion or verdict). cancel_pending and already_settled write nothing and do not call core.cancel, so a repeated cancel no longer raises the K8 revision. Breaking: cancelDelegation on a resolved delegation resolves already_settled instead of rejecting with 'Delegation already resolved'. cancelDelegation, and cancelTurn on a chain Turn, refuse with the new DelegationError (key = delegation id): unknown_delegation, and not_cancellable for a reply_held or uncertain delegation (end it with abandonDelegation). failStuckIntent refuses with HostIntentError: unknown_intent, already_settled, or not_stuck; HostIntentError gains the codes already_settled and not_stuck. The messages stay the same and both classes extend Error. A Bot Turn settled by failStuckIntent records settleCode: 'outcome_failed' on the Turn, in the ledger and its bot-turn projection; the audit row stays. The field is optional, so an older K8 reads the ledger and ignores it: a rollback keeps working, but the older K8 writes no settleCode. index.ts now exports DelegationError, HostIntentError, DelegationCancelResult, HostIntentCancelResult and TurnCancelResult. A Host that vendored K8 copies src/host.ts, src/index.ts, src/delegation.ts, src/rules/delegation.ts and src/rules/turn.ts, and switches on error.code instead of message prefixes such as 'Intent already settled'. Added (#1407): the read-only inputRoot(key, botId) returns the Turn id that input returned for that key from the ledger's command record, or undefined when the input is not committed; it runs no process() pass, writes nothing and leaves the K8 revision unchanged, so a Host can tell whether an input that rejected on its drain committed. It is in src/host.ts, which the copy list above already names.
